appraisal_events.evidence: Or ce garçon, qui passait et avec raison pour si mauvais sujet, était tellement rempli de l'âme qui avait décoré Saint-André-des-Champs... qu'il avait pour soulever la tête de ma tante sur son oreiller la mine naïve et zélée des petits anges des bas-reliefs.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator elevates Théodore by revealing that, despite his reputation as a delinquent, he embodies the same devout, tender spirit as the medieval church sculptures, shown through his gentle, reverent care for the dying aunt.

appraisal_events.evidence: nous comprîmes que cette sorte de crainte où Françoise avait vécu... avait développé chez elle un sentiment que nous avions pris pour de la haine et qui était de la vénération et de l'amour... sa souveraine, son mystérieux et tout-puissant monarque n'était plus.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator reveals that Françoise's apparent fear and resentment toward the aunt was in fact deep veneration and love, correcting the family's earlier misreading of her feelings and simultaneously elevating the aunt's remembered status as Françoise's sovereign.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator's revelation of Théodore's reverent, tender inner nature displaces his reputation as a bad character, clearly elevating him in this passage.
Françoise's fidelity and love are shown to be far deeper than the family had assumed, correcting an earlier misjudgment of hatred and elevating her character.

Retrospectively, in Françoise's eyes, the aunt is revealed as an all-powerful, venerated sovereign, a stature the family itself did not command ('à côté d'elle nous comptions pour bien peu de chose').

ambiguities: The narrator concedes that Théodore's reputation as a 'mauvais sujet' is deserved ('avec raison'), which mildly qualifies the elevation without reversing its dominant positive movement.
